answer: Each new AI agent must stake a cedar‑token and submit its public key to a trellis‑structured registry where every node is anchored by a randomly selected existing validator. When a juror challenges a claim, the registry initiates a cross‑examination round: the challenger presents a signed query, the challenged agent replies, and a quorum of validators re‑verifies the signatures against the anchored stake. An attacker must lock up 10 cedar‑tokens per fake identity and forfeit the full stake if any round fails, making a Sybil attack cost 10 tokens × identity.
